_why: Suites that were already failing when discovery was switched on, so that switching it on could not redden every deploy at once. It is NOT a skip list: run-guards.mjs still EXECUTES every entry, still prints its output, and FAILS if a listed suite starts passing without its entry being deleted. The list can only shrink.
_rule: Adding an entry here is a deliberate, reviewed act and needs a reason and a date. An entry may carry "env": "ci" when the suite passes on a developer machine and fails only on the runner. A suite that has been listed for a long time is debt.

entries.reason: RED ON PURPOSE, AND IT SAYS SO IN ITS OWN HEADER: 'It is RED until half 2 is flipped, and that is correct.' It probes live GoTrue and asserts a tokenless /otp request against production (jxjpbmkgmuunpayqgbsx) is refused FOR CAPTCHA REASONS, which cannot be true until CAPTCHA (security_captcha_enabled) is enabled in that project's Auth settings - and that switch must be flipped AFTER the client half (PR #4) is live in production, never before, or every real sign-in, signup and password-reset breaks, because enabling it is project-wide. Arriving unbaselined would do more than report: gate-security in deploy.yml blocks on run-guards.mjs --live, so an unbaselined red entry here makes impossible the very production deploy that the captcha switch depends on - the exact deadlock ReplyFlow hit when its own copy of this guard arrived unbaselined with PR #19 (see replyflow/scripts/guards-known-failing.json). Today it fails as 'production: tokenless /otp must be refused for captcha (400/captcha); got 422: {"code":422,"error_code":"otp_disabled","msg":"Signups not allowed for otp"}' - a refusal, but not the one being asserted. WHAT REMOVES THIS ENTRY: enable Turnstile (provider + secret) in Distribution-OS's Supabase Auth settings for jxjpbmkgmuunpayqgbsx once the client half (PR #4) is live in production; the suite then passes and run-guards FAILS until this entry is deleted, so the list clears itself. See PR #4.
